_about: The standard drive cycles bundled with LightSim (backend/app/cycles.py), built by
scripts/cycles/build_cycles.py. Each id has a <id>.csv trace (t_s, speed_kmh and,
where the road climbs, grade_pct). 'register' is its row in docs/data-register.csv;
'source' the document it was taken from and 'reuse' the reason LightSim may ship it
(docs/DATA-REGISTER.md lists the bases); 'phases' are [name, start s, end s];
'published' the [duration s, distance km] its source states, where one does;
'fingerprint' the sum of its 1 Hz speeds in km/h and the SHA-256 of its CSV, which
test_cycles.py recomputes. Never change a shipped trace in place: a changed cycle
gets a new id, so a run stored with the old one can still be reproduced.

wltc-3b.name: WLTC class 3b
wltc-3b.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Tables A1/7, A1/9, A1/11, A1/12. Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h
wltc-3b.note: Most cars: over 34 W/kg and a top speed of 120 km/h or more.

wltc-3a.name: WLTC class 3a
wltc-3a.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Tables A1/7, A1/8, A1/10, A1/12. Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h
wltc-3a.note: Over 34 W/kg with a top speed under 120 km/h.

wltc-2.name: WLTC class 2
wltc-2.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Tables A1/3 to A1/6. Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h
wltc-2.note: 22 to 34 W/kg (small, low-powered cars and vans).

wltc-1.name: WLTC class 1
wltc-1.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Tables A1/1, A1/2 and A1/1 again. Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h

wltc-3b-city.name: WLTC city, class 3b
wltc-3b-city.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Tables A1/7 and A1/9 (paragraph 3.5). Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h
wltc-3b-city.note: Low and Medium phases only: the city cycle electric and plug-in cars are also tested on.

wltc-3a-city.name: WLTC city, class 3a
wltc-3a-city.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Tables A1/7 and A1/8 (paragraph 3.5). Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h

wltc-3-low.name: WLTC class 3, Low phase
wltc-3-low.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Table A1/7. Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h
wltc-3-low.note: One phase on its own, from 0 to 589 s of class 3a and 3b.

wltc-3a-medium.name: WLTC class 3a, Medium phase
wltc-3a-medium.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Table A1/8. Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h

wltc-3b-medium.name: WLTC class 3b, Medium phase
wltc-3b-medium.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Table A1/9. Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h

wltc-3a-high.name: WLTC class 3a, High phase
wltc-3a-high.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Table A1/10. Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h

wltc-3b-high.name: WLTC class 3b, High phase
wltc-3b-high.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Table A1/11. Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h

wltc-3-extra-high.name: WLTC class 3, Extra High phase
wltc-3-extra-high.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1151, Annex XXI, Sub-Annex 1, Table A1/12. Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h
wltc-3-extra-high.note: One phase on its own, the same for class 3a and 3b.

nedc.name: NEDC (withdrawn)
nedc.source: UN/ECE Regulation No 83 as published in OJ L 42, 15.2.2012, Annex 4a, Tables 1 and 2 (manual-gearbox operations). Source: EUR-Lex, © European Union; converted to a CSV in km/h
nedc.note: Replaced by WLTP for new cars from 2017-2019; for comparing with older published figures. The gear changes hold their speed for 2 s, as the regulation's tables say.

udds.name: EPA city (UDDS)
udds.source: 40 CFR Part 86, Appendix I; EPA's uddscol.txt
udds.note: The city cycle of EPA fuel-economy tests (also called LA4 or FTP-72).

hwfet.name: EPA highway (HWFET)
hwfet.source: 40 CFR Part 600, Appendix I; EPA's hwycol.txt
hwfet.note: The highway cycle of EPA fuel-economy tests.

ftp-75.name: EPA FTP-75 (without the soak)
ftp-75.source: 40 CFR Part 86, Appendix I, and 86.137; EPA's ftpcol.txt
ftp-75.note: The UDDS and a repeat of its first 505 s. The real test parks the car for 10 minutes before Bag 3; this trace leaves the soak out, and LightSim does not model the cold start.

us06.name: EPA US06
us06.source: 40 CFR Part 86, Appendix I; EPA's us06col.txt
us06.note: Hard accelerations and high speed: one of EPA's supplemental (five-cycle) tests.

sc03.name: EPA SC03
sc03.source: 40 CFR Part 86, Appendix I; EPA's sc03col.txt
sc03.note: The air-conditioning test of EPA's five-cycle method (run at 35 °C with sun in the real test).

la92.name: LA92 (Unified cycle, hot)
la92.source: EPA's la92dds.txt (the first 1,435 s of the LA92 Dynamometer Driving Schedule)
la92.note: Faster than the FTP, with fewer stops; used by California's air board and for heavy-duty class 3 vehicles.

ftp-mc-1b.name: EPA motorcycle FTP, class I-B
ftp-mc-1b.source: 40 CFR Part 86, Appendix I; EPA's ftpmc1b.txt
ftp-mc-1b.note: The FTP with lower speeds from 164 to 332 s and from 1,533 to 1,701 s, for motorcycles of 50 to 169 cc; without the 10-minute soak.

wmtc.name: WMTC (motorcycles, parts 1-3)
wmtc.source: UN GTR No. 2 (WMTC), as shipped in FASTSim 2.1.5 (wmtc_all.csv)
wmtc.note: The world motorcycle test cycle, all three parts (the version for the fastest class).

wmtc-part1.name: WMTC part 1
wmtc-part1.source: UN GTR No. 2 (WMTC), as shipped in FASTSim 2.1.5 (wmtc_part1.csv)

wmtc-part2.name: WMTC part 2
wmtc-part2.source: UN GTR No. 2 (WMTC), as shipped in FASTSim 2.1.5 (wmtc_part2.csv)

wmtc-part3.name: WMTC part 3
wmtc-part3.source: UN GTR No. 2 (WMTC), as shipped in FASTSim 2.1.5 (wmtc_part3.csv)

long-haul.name: Long-haul truck route (804.6 km, with grade)
long-haul.note: A 23-hour truck trip with the road's grade (from -2.3 to +2.9 %). A run takes a long time; start with the 100 km excerpt.

long-haul-100km.name: Long-haul truck route, first 100 km (with grade)
long-haul-100km.source: The first 100 km of FASTSim 2.1.5 longHaulDriveCycle.csv (NREL)
long-haul-100km.note: Ends at speed where the route passes 100 km.
